entries.author: teacher
entries.content: The root cause was in `ExpressionChecker.visit_index_with_type` (mypy/checkexpr.py): when the base of an index expression `data["x"]` had a `TypeVarType`, mypy fell through to the generic `__getitem__` method-call path, which resolves the member through the TypedDict's fallback type (`Mapping[str, object]`), producing `object` instead of using the TypedDict-specific indexing logic that knows key `"x"` is an `int`. The fix adds a `TypeVarType` branch that re-analyzes the index operation against the type variable's upper bound (keeping the original type variable for error messages via `original_type`), so TypedDict bounds get proper key checking, and tuple/enum/union bounds also benefit from their respective special cases. Verified with the issue's example, additional edge cases (invalid keys, union/tuple bounds, unbounded TypeVars with unchanged error messages), and the full `testcheck` suite (5406 passed).
